scenes.headline: A meeting invite you didn't expect?
scenes.say: Got a meeting invite you didn't expect? It could be a trap.

scenes.headline: fake calendar-invite emails flagged
scenes.say: Check Point researchers flagged over three hundred thousand fake calendar invite emails, sent to more than forty thousand organisations.

scenes.headline: Steal your Microsoft 365 login
scenes.body: The invite points you to a fake sign-in page.
scenes.say: The goal: steal your Microsoft three sixty five login, through a fake sign-in page.

scenes.headline: The file is real calendar data
scenes.body: No software bug. It abuses your trust.
scenes.say: Why does it work? The invite file is real calendar data. No software bug. It abuses calendar features, and your trust.

scenes.headline: A sudden surge
scenes.say: The surge began on September twenty-fifth. On October eighth alone, almost two hundred thousand emails went out.

scenes.headline: A Join button is just a link.
scenes.body: A calendar entry is not proof a meeting is real.
scenes.say: Analyst note: a Join button is just a link. A calendar entry is not proof a meeting is real.

scenes.headline: Do this today
items: Report it to your IT team
scenes.say: Today: if an invite is unexpected, don't click Join. Open Teams or Outlook yourself. And report it to your IT team.

scenes.headline: The security story behind the headline.
scenes.say: Sources are in the description. Follow Securidge.
